findings.description: The "call-tree or call-stack change" worked diff example removes and re-adds the identical, unchanged line `navigateToSession` (a no-op `-`/`+` pair), contradicting the section's own instruction to "match the diff shape to the topic" and teaching agents the wrong convention for showing a new child added under an unchanged parent.
findings.body:
This worked example is meant to teach an agent the right `diff` shape for a call-tree change, but it shows a no-op `-`/`+` pair on identical text:

```diff
 submitForm
   createSession
     persistPrompt
+    expandSkillMention
     launchAgent
-  navigateToSession
+  navigateToSession
+    subscribeToEvents
```

`navigateToSession` is removed and re-added with byte-identical text and indentation — a diff a real tool would never produce, and exactly what the section's own guidance one screen above ("Use `diff` when the point is what changes... Match the diff shape to the topic") argues against. None of the file's other four worked diff examples use a same-text `-`/`+` pair; they all keep unchanged lines as plain context and mark only genuinely different lines (e.g. the component-tree example keeps `<SessionToolbar>` unmarked and only `+`-marks the new `<RunSkillButton />`). Since this is a worked example an agent will pattern-match against when drafting a real PR Summary, it actively teaches the wrong lesson.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/0f2f2fcba7b2d9836dbafa08e335a7e8d760c8b0/.claude/skills/pr-description/SKILL.md#L119-L128
findings.suggestion:
```diff
 submitForm
   createSession
     persistPrompt
+    expandSkillMention
     launchAgent
   navigateToSession
+    subscribeToEvents
```

findings.description: The attribution sentence "The Summary views are adapted from Dex Horthy's `show-me` skill (humanlayer/skills)" sits as an unmarked trailing paragraph inside `## Body rules` (the file's last section), directly beneath a bullet that says "Never add ... any agent attribution ... to the PR body" — no heading or separator marks it as meta-commentary about the skill file itself rather than PR-body content.

The "follow-up to a prior PR" worked-example title (`chore(skills): take the template's implement and wayfinder skills (follow-up to #93)`) is 84 characters, over the "≲ 80 chars" rule stated three lines above it — the one example meant to model a compliant title exceeds the limit it illustrates.

process_issues.description: Neither reviewer brief mentioned that .claude/ is config-restored to the base branch in the working tree under CI, so a plain Read on .claude/skills/pr-description/SKILL.md serves stale (pre-delta) content. Both the conventions and docs reviewers independently discovered this and correctly worked around it via `git show HEAD:<path>`, so it did not degrade this run, but the brief should include this caveat going forward to avoid relying on reviewers rediscovering it.
